checks.label: Airplane Mode
checks.description: Airplane mode status
checks.remediation: Toggle airplane mode via: settings put global airplane_mode_on 1 (enable) or 0 (disable).

checks.label: Mobile Data Enabled
checks.description: Mobile data status
checks.remediation: Disable mobile data if not needed: svc data disable

checks.label: High Port Listeners (3000+)
checks.command: (netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null || ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null) | grep LISTEN | grep -oE ':[0-9]+' | sed 's/://' | awk '$1>=3000' | sort -nu | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//'
checks.description: Listening on high ports (3000+) - may indicate backdoor, C2 server, or dev tools
checks.remediation: Identify and stop the process using each port: fuser -k <port>/tcp. Remove or disable the responsible app.

checks.label: Data Roaming
checks.description: Data roaming can incur costs and security risks
checks.remediation: Disable data roaming: settings put global data_roaming 0

checks.label: Preferred Network Mode
checks.description: Preferred cellular network mode
checks.remediation: Set preferred network mode to LTE/5G only to avoid downgrade attacks: settings put global preferred_network_mode 11

checks.label: VoLTE Enabled
checks.description: Voice over LTE status
checks.remediation: Review VoLTE setting in device Settings > Network > Mobile Network > VoLTE calls.

checks.label: DNS Servers
checks.description: Check DNS configs
checks.remediation: Set a trusted DNS server: setprop net.dns1 1.1.1.1 or use Private DNS in settings.

checks.label: Wi-Fi Security (WPA3)
checks.command: WIFI=$(settings get global wifi_on 2>/dev/null); [ "$WIFI" = "1" ] && dumpsys wifi 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'WPA[23][^," ]*' | head -3 || echo 'wifi_off'
checks.description: WPA3 should be preferred over WPA2 for stronger Wi-Fi security. Check skipped when Wi-Fi is off.
checks.remediation: Connect only to WPA3-enabled networks. Upgrade your router firmware to support WPA3 if possible.

checks.label: DNS-over-TLS Enabled
checks.description: DNS-over-TLS (DoT) should be enabled. Both 'hostname' (strict) and 'opportunistic' modes provide encrypted DNS.
checks.remediation: Enable Private DNS: settings put global private_dns_mode hostname && settings put global private_dns_specifier dns.google

checks.label: ARP Table Dump
checks.description: Lists resolved ARP IP-MAC mappings
checks.remediation: Review ARP entries for unexpected devices. Flush stale entries: ip neigh flush all

checks.label: Proxy Configuration
checks.description: Proxy set may indicate MITM or forced redirection
checks.remediation: Remove the proxy: settings put global http_proxy :0 or settings delete global http_proxy

checks.label: Captive Portal Detection
checks.description: Should be 1 (default); 0 disables captive portal checks
checks.remediation: Re-enable captive portal detection: settings put global captive_portal_mode 1

checks.label: Firebase Config Present
checks.description: Firebase configuration - check security rules
checks.remediation: Audit Firebase security rules in the Firebase Console. Ensure Realtime DB and Firestore rules deny public read/write.

checks.label: AWS SDK/Config
checks.description: AWS credentials or config found
checks.remediation: Remove hardcoded AWS credentials from device. Use IAM roles or AWS IoT certificates instead of static keys.

checks.label: Azure IoT Config
checks.description: Azure IoT Hub configuration found
checks.remediation: Remove plaintext Azure connection strings. Use x509 certificates or TPM-based device provisioning instead.

checks.label: MQTT Broker Config
checks.description: MQTT broker configuration files
checks.remediation: Ensure MQTT uses TLS (mqtts:// on port 8883) with username/password or client certificates. Disable anonymous access.

checks.label: Telemetry Endpoints
checks.description: Telemetry/analytics endpoints configured
checks.remediation: Review and disable unnecessary telemetry. Block telemetry domains via Private DNS or firewall rules.

checks.label: OTA Update URL
checks.description: OTA update configuration - verify HTTPS and signing
checks.remediation: Verify OTA URLs use HTTPS. Confirm firmware images require signature verification before installation.

checks.label: Remote Management Ports
checks.description: Management/API ports exposed
checks.remediation: Stop unnecessary management services. Bind them to 127.0.0.1 only or use iptables to restrict access.

checks.label: Open TCP Ports
checks.description: All listening TCP ports - review for unnecessary services
checks.remediation: Close unnecessary listening ports. Stop or uninstall the service, or bind to 127.0.0.1 if local-only access is needed.

checks.label: Open UDP Ports
checks.description: INFO: All external UDP ports. 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output exposes UDP services. Why: UDP services often lack authentication.
checks.remediation: Disable unneeded UDP services. Use iptables -A INPUT -p udp --dport <port> -j DROP to block specific ports.

checks.label: HTTP Server Running
checks.description: Web server exposed - potential attack surface
checks.remediation: Stop the web server process if not needed. If required, bind to 127.0.0.1 and enforce HTTPS with valid certificates.

checks.label: Telnet Service (Insecure)
checks.description: Telnet transmits credentials in plaintext - CRITICAL RISK
checks.remediation: Disable telnet immediately: stop the telnetd service and remove the binary. Replace with SSH.

checks.label: FTP Service (Insecure)
checks.description: FTP transmits credentials in plaintext - CRITICAL RISK
checks.remediation: Disable FTP immediately: stop the ftpd service and remove the binary. Replace with SFTP or SCP.

checks.label: SSH Service
checks.description: SSH exposed - ensure strong authentication
checks.remediation: Disable SSH if not needed. If required, use key-based auth only and disable root login in sshd_config.

checks.label: ADB Network Port (5555)
checks.description: ADB over network - allows remote shell access!
checks.remediation: Disable ADB over network immediately: adb tcpip -1 or setprop service.adb.tcp.port -1 && stop adbd && start adbd

checks.label: MQTT Broker (1883/8883)
checks.description: MQTT broker exposed - check authentication
checks.remediation: Enable MQTT authentication and use TLS on port 8883. Disable anonymous access in the broker config.

checks.label: CoAP Service (5683/5684)
checks.description: CoAP service exposed - IoT protocol
checks.remediation: Use CoAPS (DTLS) on port 5684 instead of plaintext CoAP. Restrict access with firewall rules.

checks.label: UPnP Service (1900)
checks.description: UPnP can expose device to network attacks
checks.remediation: Disable UPnP/SSDP service. Stop the process listening on port 1900 and prevent it from restarting.

checks.label: Network Interfaces
checks.description: Active network interfaces and IPs
checks.remediation: Disable unused network interfaces: ip link set <interface> down. Reduce the attack surface.

checks.label: Default Gateway
checks.description: Network gateway configuration
checks.remediation: Verify the default gateway is your trusted router. Unexpected gateways may indicate ARP spoofing.

checks.label: Network Services Exposed
checks.description: Network services exposed - each must be documented and secured
checks.remediation: Stop all non-essential exposed services. Bind remaining services to 127.0.0.1 or use iptables to whitelist IPs.

checks.label: WiFi Security Protocol
checks.description: Must use WPA2/WPA3 - WEP/Open networks prohibited for PHI
checks.remediation: Disconnect from WEP/Open networks. Remove them from saved networks: cmd wifi forget-network <networkId>

checks.label: Root Network Access Test
checks.description: INFO: Tests if root access works for network commands. If ROOT_REQUIRED shown, run HARDAX on rooted device for full network audit.
checks.remediation: Root the device or use adb shell with elevated privileges for a complete network audit.

checks.label: All Network Connections (Root)
checks.description: INFO: Complete network connections list. Shows all TCP/UDP with PID if rooted. Use to verify other checks are working.
checks.remediation: Review all connections and terminate suspicious ones. Kill offending processes: kill -9 <PID>

checks.label: Listening Ports Summary (Root)
checks.description: INFO: All listening ports (TCP+UDP). 🟢 SAFE=only 127.0.0.1. 🔴 REVIEW=any 0.0.0.0 or external IP. Shows PID/program if rooted.
checks.remediation: Rebind services on 0.0.0.0 to 127.0.0.1. Stop any service you do not recognize or need.

checks.label: Listening TCP Ports (IPv4)
checks.description: INFO: All IPv4 TCP listening ports. 🟢 SAFE if 127.0.0.1 (localhost only). 🔴 UNSAFE if 0.0.0.0 (anyone can connect). Empty may indicate command failure on non-rooted device.
checks.remediation: Close ports bound to 0.0.0.0. Reconfigure services to listen on 127.0.0.1 only.

checks.label: Common TCP Ports Exposed (IPv4)
checks.description: WARNING: 22(SSH), 53(DNS), 80(HTTP), 8080(Proxy) exposed! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: brute force, unencrypted traffic.
checks.remediation: Disable exposed common services or restrict with iptables: iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport <port> -j DROP

checks.label: Critical TCP Ports Exposed (IPv4)
checks.description: CRITICAL: 21(FTP), 23(Telnet), 5555(ADB), 3306(MySQL), 3389(RDP), 5900(VNC) exposed! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED!
checks.remediation: Immediately stop FTP, Telnet, ADB, and VNC services. Block these ports: iptables -A INPUT -p tcp -m multiport --dports 21,23,5555,5900 -j DROP

checks.label: Open UDP Ports (IPv4, excluding localhost)
checks.command: netstat -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep '^udp ' | grep -v '127\.' || ss -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep '^udp' | grep -v '127\.'
checks.description: INFO: External UDP ports. 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: UDP services often lack authentication.
checks.remediation: Stop unnecessary UDP services. Block with: iptables -A INPUT -p udp --dport <port> -j DROP

checks.label: UDP Ports 123, 161, 162, 5353 Open (IPv4)
checks.description: WARNING: 123(NTP), 161(SNMP), 5353(mDNS) exposed! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: DDoS amplification, device info leakage.
checks.remediation: Disable SNMP and mDNS if not needed. Restrict NTP to client-only mode. Block ports with iptables.

checks.label: Potentially Vulnerable UDP Ports (IPv4)
checks.description: CRITICAL: 69(TFTP), 1900(SSDP), 500(IPsec) exposed! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: No auth, DDoS amplification!
checks.remediation: Stop TFTP and SSDP services immediately. Block ports: iptables -A INPUT -p udp -m multiport --dports 69,1900,520 -j DROP

checks.label: Expanded Critical TCP Ports (excluding SSH) Listening or External (IPv6)
checks.description: CRITICAL: Dangerous ports on IPv6! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: Full device control via IPv6!
checks.remediation: Stop dangerous services on IPv6. Apply ip6tables rules: ip6tables -A INPUT -p tcp -m multiport --dports 21,23,5555,5900 -j DROP

checks.label: Open UDP Ports (IPv6, excluding localhost)
checks.command: netstat -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep '^udp6' | grep -v '::1' || ss -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep 'udp6\|\[::\]' | grep -v '::1'
checks.description: INFO: External IPv6 UDP ports. 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: Bypasses IPv4 firewall rules.
checks.remediation: Disable IPv6 if not needed: sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1. Otherwise apply ip6tables rules.

checks.label: UDP Ports 123, 161, 162, 5353 Open (IPv6)
checks.command: netstat -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep '^udp6' | grep -E ':(123|161|162|5353)[^0-9]' | grep -v '::1' || ss -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep 'udp6' | grep -E ':(123|161|5353)[^0-9]' | grep -v '::1'
checks.description: WARNING: NTP/SNMP/mDNS on IPv6! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: DDoS, device discovery.
checks.remediation: Disable SNMP/mDNS on IPv6. Block with: ip6tables -A INPUT -p udp -m multiport --dports 123,161,5353 -j DROP

checks.label: Potentially Vulnerable UDP Ports (IPv6)
checks.command: netstat -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep '^udp6' | grep -E ':(69|1900|500|4500|520)[^0-9]' | grep -v '::1' || ss -lnup 2>/dev/null | grep 'udp6' | grep -E ':(69|1900)[^0-9]' | grep -v '::1'
checks.description: CRITICAL: TFTP/SSDP on IPv6! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: No-auth file transfer, DDoS!
checks.remediation: Stop TFTP/SSDP on IPv6 immediately. Block: ip6tables -A INPUT -p udp -m multiport --dports 69,1900 -j DROP

checks.label: VPN Legacy Mode
checks.description: Legacy VPN mode status
checks.remediation: Disable legacy VPN mode if enabled: settings put global vpn_legacy_mode 0. Use modern VPN protocols.

checks.label: Always-On VPN
checks.description: Always-on VPN app if configured
checks.remediation: Configure always-on VPN in Settings > Network > VPN > select your VPN > enable Always-on VPN.

checks.label: VPN Lockdown
checks.description: VPN lockdown mode prevents traffic without VPN
checks.remediation: Enable VPN lockdown: settings put secure always_on_vpn_lockdown 1 to block all traffic when VPN is disconnected.

checks.label: Active VPN Connections
checks.description: Current VPN connection status
checks.remediation: Ensure a VPN is active on untrusted networks. Configure always-on VPN for persistent protection.

checks.label: WiFi Enabled
checks.description: WiFi enabled status
checks.remediation: Disable WiFi when not in use: svc wifi disable. This reduces the wireless attack surface.

checks.label: WiFi Networks Saved
checks.description: Number of saved WiFi networks
checks.remediation: Remove old or untrusted saved networks: cmd wifi forget-network <networkId>. Fewer saved networks reduces risk.

checks.label: WiFi MAC Randomization
checks.description: MAC randomization protects privacy
checks.remediation: Enable MAC randomization: settings put global wifi_connected_mac_randomization_enabled 1

checks.label: WiFi Scan Always Available
checks.description: WiFi scanning when WiFi off can leak location
checks.remediation: Disable background WiFi scanning: settings put global wifi_scan_always_enabled 0

checks.label: Open Network Notification
checks.description: Notifications for open networks
checks.remediation: Disable open network notifications: settings put global wifi_networks_available_notification_on 0

checks.label: WiFi Watchdog
checks.description: WiFi watchdog monitors connection quality
checks.remediation: Enable WiFi watchdog: settings put global wifi_watchdog_on 1

checks.label: WiFi Captive Portal Detection
checks.description: Captive portal detection for public WiFi
checks.remediation: Enable captive portal detection: settings put global captive_portal_detection_enabled 1

checks.label: Active External Connections (ESTABLISHED)
checks.command: netstat -tunp 2>/dev/null | grep ESTABLISHED | grep -vE '127.0.0.1|::1|localhost' | head -20 || ss -tunp 2>/dev/null | grep ESTAB | grep -vE '127.0.0.1|::1' | head -20
checks.description: Active outbound connections to external IPs - unexpected connections may indicate C2 communication or data exfiltration
checks.remediation: Investigate unknown external connections. Kill suspicious processes: kill -9 <PID>. Block IPs with iptables.

checks.label: Listening TCP Ports (IPv6, excluding ::1)
checks.command: netstat -lntp 2>/dev/null | grep '^tcp6' | grep -v '::1' || ss -lntp 2>/dev/null | grep 'tcp6\|\[::\]' | grep -v '::1'
checks.description: INFO: IPv6 TCP listening ports. 🟢 SAFE=empty or ::1 only. 🔴 UNSAFE if ::: (all interfaces). IPv6 often overlooked!
checks.remediation: Close unnecessary IPv6 listeners. Apply ip6tables rules or disable IPv6: sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1

checks.label: Common TCP Ports Exposed (IPv6, Warning)
checks.description: WARNING: Common TCP on IPv6! 🟢 SAFE=empty. 🔴 UNSAFE=any output. Risk: Often missed in firewall rules!
checks.remediation: Apply ip6tables rules matching your iptables rules. Block exposed ports: ip6tables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport <port> -j DROP

checks.label: Allow 2G Disabled (Android 14+)
checks.description: Android 14 introduces a per-SIM toggle to disable 2G. Disabling 2G prevents cellular-downgrade attacks where a rogue base station forces a device onto unauthenticated GSM. Critical for cellular POS terminals and any device handling sensitive traffic over mobile data.
checks.remediation: On Android 14+, set under Settings > Network & internet > SIMs > Allow 2G off, or run: 'settings put global cell_2g_allowed 0'. On older Android, this control is not available.

checks.label: Hotspot WPA Mode
checks.description: If the device hosts a Wi-Fi hotspot it should run WPA2 or WPA3 (SAE), never Open or WEP. Empty output means the hotspot is not active, which is also acceptable. Critical for any device that may act as an access point in the field.
checks.remediation: If a hotspot is in use, configure it for WPA2-Personal or WPA3-Personal (SAE) under Settings > Network & internet > Hotspot & tethering.
